summary: The note examines rising greenhouse gas emissions from local transport and their environmental and public health toll, citing a 9% year-on-year increase reported in September 2023. It breaks down the pollutants (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide), describes health impacts such as respiratory and cardiovascular disease, and outlines responses including the Green Transport Initiative, the Commuter Revamp Project, RideShare Week, the Urban Sustainability Framework and economic arguments for green transport.
one_line: Local transport greenhouse gas emissions are rising and harming public health, prompting government, community, planning and economic efforts to reduce them.
key_facts: The Municipal Department of Environmental Health reported on September 15, 2023 a 9% year-on-year increase in emissions from private and public transportation in the local area.
The Environmental Traffic Monitor, led by Clean Air Local Initiative on October 3, 2023, found the average commuter contributes approximately 4.6 metric tons of CO2 annually.
Methane is approximately 25 times more potent than CO2 over a century at absorbing heat.
Nitrous oxide is 300 times more potent than carbon dioxide and stays in the atmosphere for over a century.
Dr. Rajiv Narayan said on December 20, 2023 that hospital admissions for asthma and other lung conditions spike on days when vehicular emissions peak.
The Public Health and Transportation Alliance study of January 4, 2024, led by Dr. Lara Thompson, linked traffic-related air pollution to elevated lung cancer, stroke and heart attacks.
The Green Transport Initiative, launched by the local government on February 1, 2024, aims to cut local transport emissions by 25% over five years.
The Green Transport Initiative introduced electric buses and tax incentives for citizens choosing electric or hybrid personal vehicles.
The Commuter Revamp Project targets mid-2025 completion and includes expanding bus lanes, optimizing transit schedules and upgrading aging fleets to fuel-efficient models.
RideShare Week, inaugurated on March 17, 2024, promotes carpooling; campaigner Julia Henderson says sharing journeys halves travel emissions.
The Urban Sustainability Framework, released April 2, 2024, promotes mixed-use neighborhoods, pedestrian-friendly zones and cycling paths.

The Advocate for Sustainable Economics reported on May 10, 2024 that cutting transport emissions could bring gains via reduced healthcare costs, enhanced worker productivity and improved market positioning.
